title: Building Foundation Models via Weight-Space Programming (WSP): Analytical Alignment, Multi-Donor Cognitive Grafting, and Closed-Form Refusal Abliteration without Backpropagation

target_networks.name: Quillan-Ronin Sovereign 1.2B (merged from Llama 3.2 1B, Falcon 3 1B, BitNet 1.58b, Qwen 2.5)

domain: LLM model merging, refusal removal and edge deployment

headline_result.text: A merged 1.2B model with refusal-direction ablation, built without gradients, runs at 48.0 tokens/s on a GTX 1050 (12.18x a PyTorch baseline); no task accuracy is reported.
headline_result.quote: WSP synthesizes a calibrated Sovereign 1.2B foundation model in under 180 seconds, achieving 48.0 tokens/second generation throughput (a 12.18× acceleration over uncompiled PyTorch baselines) with zero corporate refusal evasion.

key_claims.claim: The paper redefines WSP as deterministic, gradient-free analytical editing of weights and covariances, with no LLM acting as editor.
key_claims.quote: we formalize Weight-Space Programming (WSP): a deterministic, analytical framework that constructs, aligns, grafts, and compresses foundation models entirely in weight and activation covariance spaces without calculating a single gradient

key_claims.claim: Refusal is removed by projecting down-projection weights away from a difference-of-means refusal direction in layers 12 to 15.
key_claims.quote: we project the SwiGLU down-projection weights Wdown onto the orthogonal null space of vrefusal across layers 12 through 15

key_claims.claim: Low-rank adapters from four donor models are merged into a MoE that is then folded into one dense matrix under uniform routing.
key_claims.quote: If routing is uniform with scaling factor γ and expert weight 1/K, the dynamic MoE layer is identical to a single folded linear transformation

key_claims.claim: The reported speedup compares a Q4_K_M GGUF build with an FP16 PyTorch baseline, so precision and runtime change together.
key_claims.quote: Quillan-Ronin Sovereign GGUF (WSP) Q4_K_M 1,024 MB 48.00 tok/s 12.18x (Peak)

notes_for_review: This 5-page document uses the WSP label for classical abliteration (difference-of-means direction projection), adapter merging and quantized export; no language model reads or writes weights, so it is not WSP in the MIT sense. No accuracy, capability or safety evaluation is reported, only throughput, and the 12.18x speedup confounds 4-bit GGUF with FP16 PyTorch. It is useful only as an example of the term being borrowed for unrelated work.
